evidence.excerpt: Vapour permeability was measured for EPDM, silicone, and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) seal materials in unaged condition and after accelerated thermal ageing (100 °C, 1000 hours) and UV ageing (1.0 W/m² at 340 nm, 500 hours) in accordance with ISO 4892-2. Gravimetric cup tests at 23 °C and 85 % relative humidity differential were conducted on three specimens per material per ageing condition. EPDM permeability increased by 12 % after thermal ageing and by 8 % after UV ageing relative to the unaged baseline. Silicone showed no statistically significant change after thermal ageing but a 19 % increase after UV ageing. TPU exhibited the largest sensitivity, with permeability increasing by 34 % after thermal ageing and 27 % after UV ageing, accompanied by visible surface crazing and a 15 % reduction in hardness. Shore A hardness, tensile elongation at break, and infrared spectroscopy were used to characterise degradation mechanisms. The results indicate that TPU is not recommended for long-service-life outdoor enclosures exposed to solar radiation.
